 1                 ACTING PRESIDENT BAILEY:   Majority 

 2    Leader Andrea Stewart-Cousins on the resolution.

 3                 SENATOR STEWART-COUSINS:   Thank 

 4    you, Mr. President.  

 5                 I rise and this time I want to make 

 6    sure that I thank our chair of Veterans and 

 7    Homeland Security, Senator Scarcella-Spanton, as 

 8    well as the ranker, Senator Ashby, as well as all 

 9    of our colleagues, but certainly Senator 

10    Scarcella-Spanton for helping to put together our 

11    20th recognition of veterans by this chamber.

12                 It is extraordinary when we think 

13    that 20 years has passed since we began this 

14    recognition.  And something that Leader Ortt said 

15    this morning, I wanted to make sure that we in 

16    this chamber understood.  He thanked me for 

17    continuing the tradition of honoring the veterans 

18    that had been started before we were a majority 

19    here on this side.

20                 Had I continued that tradition, we 

21    would only have honored Democratic military 

22    people, because the original setup, basically the 

23    majority honored their veterans.  

24                 I remember getting here in 2007 with 

25    a veteran that I wanted to honor, but I couldn't, 


                                                                3962

 1    because we weren't in the majority.  And I had to 

 2    go through my Republican mayor to beg to have 

 3    this person included.  

 4                 It was during that time that I had a 

 5    Republican Senator, Tom Morahan, stand up and say 

 6    he agreed that we have to honor all of our 

 7    veterans, because service transcends political 

 8    parties.  And when we took the majority in 2009, 

 9    that's exactly what we did.

10                 So the tradition of service is 

11    honored in every quarter, in every corner of our 

12    state.  And when I looked again at the array of 

13    amazing veterans -- their heroism, their bravery, 

14    their courage, from World War II, Korean War, 

15    Vietnam, Afghanistan, as Senator Ortt has served, 

16    and so many others -- and of course, you know, 

17    I'm not talking of all of the different 

18    deployments and so on -- we have to always 

19    recognize that that service which allows us to be 

20    in these chambers has to be honored.

22    as I looked at this amazing group of people from 

23    all over the state, all different backgrounds and 

24    ethnicities, the conversation about DEI and the 

25    military.  


                                                                3963

 1                 I've stood on this floor so many 

 2    times talking about my father, who served in a 

 3    segregated Army, who -- Purple Heart, Bronze 

 4    Star -- came back to a segregated country, did

13    Vietnam War veteran, who came back and like all 

14    the veterans at that time, because the war was 

15    extremely unpopular, they were denigrated.

20    it's so-called the "Forgotten War."  Think about

18                 Today I am proud to honor my third 

19    inductee into the Veterans Hall of Fame, 

20    exceptional Staten Islander and American hero 

21    Louis Lupinacci, also formerly known as 

22    Uncle Louie on Staten Island.

23                 On December 23, 1942, Louie enlisted 

24    in the United States Army and trained at Fort 

25    Sheridan as a machine gunner.  Just two years 


                                                                3966

 1    later, he landed in the first wave at Easy Red 

 2    Beach on D-Day.  Louie fought valiantly through 

 3    the beaches of Normandy and continued his service 

 4    across Belgium, Holland, Scotland, England and 

 5    Germany, helping to secure and stabilize regions 

 6    critical to defending democracy and the world.  

 7                 When he returned home from war, he 

 8    didn't stop serving his country.  As he worked 

 9    through his own transition back to civilian life, 

10    he joined the 52-20 Club, a program that helped 

11    other veterans transition as well.

12                 Over the course of his life, Louie 

13    Lupinacci received numerous honors, including the 

14    Army Good Conduct Medal, the World War II Victory 

15    Medal, the European African Middle Eastern 

16    Campaign Medal, the Army of Occupation Medal, and 

17    the D-Day Commemorative Medal.

18                 And this past September, Louie 

19    reached an extraordinary milestone:  His 

20    100th birthday.  And he actually was up here with 

21    us today.  I have to brag about Louie.  Louie 

22    still drives.  He said that the key to life is 

23    making sure you drink wine with peaches in it.  I 

24    felt like I should pass that information -- red 

25    wine with peaches in it.  I felt like I should 


                                                                3967

 1    pass that information along to everybody.

 2                 (Laughter.)

 3                 SENATOR SCARCELLA-SPANTON:   But in 

 4    celebration, October 9th has officially been 

 5    declared Louis "Louie" Lupinacci Day on 

 6    Staten Island by our borough president.  

 7                 And I was honored to be able to take 

 8    part in his 100th birthday, because what I've 

 9    gotten to see from Uncle Louie is really how to 

10    live life and how to enjoy life.  He had so many 

11    people surrounding him.  I only met him at his 

12    birthday party, so I'm looking for someone who 

13    you would think would look like a 100-year-old, 

14    which I did not find.  He came running down the 

15    stairs to greet me and say hello as he got his 

16    proclamation.  And he ate it up, he really did.  

17                 So it was truly an honor.  He was up 

18    here with his family today.  It was an honor to 

19    have him with us.  And it's an honor to be able 

20    to serve in this committee to get stuff done for 

21    our veterans, for their families, and for people 

22    like Louie.  

23                 So thank you.  I proudly vote aye.
